ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\angle BOC=60^\circ$, $OE$ bisects $\angle AOC$, and $OF$ bisects $\angle BOC$. If $\angle AOC + \angle EOF = 210^\circ$, then how many degrees is $\angle EOF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle BOC=60^\circ$ and OF bisects $\angle BOC$,\\
it follows that $\angle COF= \frac{1}{2}\angle BOC=30^\circ$,\\
Given that OE bisects $\angle AOC$,\\
it follows that $\angle AOC=2\angle COE$,\\
Given that $\angle AOC+\angle EOF=210^\circ$,\\
it follows that $2\angle COE+\angle COE-\angle COF=210^\circ$,\\
which simplifies to $3\angle COE-30^\circ=210^\circ$,\\
and therefore $\angle COE=80^\circ$,\\
consequently, $\angle EOF=\angle COE-\angle COF=\boxed{50^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, all rays start from point O. OA is vertically upward, and OB is horizontally to the right; OE is between OA and OB and is closer to OB; OF is between OB and OC; OC is located lower. Therefore, inside the angle from OC turning toward OE, OF is in the middle, and it can be seen that ∠EOF = ∠COE - ∠COF. Reasoning: Let x = ∠COE. It is known that ∠BOC = 60°, and OF bisects ∠BOC, so ∠COF = 60° ÷ 2 = 30°. Also because OE bisects ∠AOC, ∠AOC = 2∠COE = 2x. From the given condition ∠AOC + ∠EOF = 210°, and from the positional relationship in the figure ∠EOF = x - 30°, substituting gives 2x + (x - 30°) = 210°. Simplifying gives 3x - 30° = 210°, so 3x = 240°, x = 80°. Therefore ∠EOF = x - 30° = 80° - 30° = 50°.
